nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression was used to estimate the normative range of ALFF values in healthy controls. The model was trained using age and sex as predictors. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation (100 runs), leave-one-site-out cross-validation, and cross-dataset validation. The normative model is from GAUSSIAN PROCESS REGRESSION AND CLASSIFICATION Toolbox version 4.2.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression was trained to estimate the normative range of ALFF values based on age and sex in HCs. The trained model was then applied to each patient, generating a Z-score (individualized ALFF abnormality).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Han2024B.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling individualized ALFF abnormalities

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: ALFF (amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations) was the response variable. ALFF maps were calculated using DPARSF (version 5.4) and mean ALFF values were extracted for 246 brain regions defined in the Brainnetome atlas. Combat harmonization was applied to minimize site effects.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibit aberrant spontaneous neural activity, commonly quantified through the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF)... ALFF maps were calculated with the Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF) protocol (version 5.4)... Mean ALFF values were calculated for each brain region defined in the brain connectome atlas
